newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine Q1 foreign direct investment up 14.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine Q1 foreign direct investment up 14.4 pct.

text.p: Private foreign direct invesment in Ukraine in the first three months of this year rose 14.4 percent on the same period in 1996, the Statistics Ministry said on Tuesday.
Ministry data showed foreign investment in Ukraine over January to March was $156.8 million, bringing total foreign direct investment since independence in 1991 to $1.49 billion.

The largest investors have been the U.S. ($272 million), Germany ($160 million), Netherlands ($131.9 million), Cyprus ($115.7 million), Russia ($112.7 million) and Britain ($105.4 million), the ministry said.
A total of 5,366 Ukrainian businesses have some form of foreign invesment, it said.
Food industries are the most common investment target, followed by trade, light manufacturing and machine-building.
Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko had forecast last week that total foreign invesment this year could rise to $800 million against $458.9 million in 1996.
